([[Scarborough, Toronto|Scarborough, Ontario]]) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Joshua Primo''' (born December 24, 2002) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. ==High school career== Primo played basketball for [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]], where he was teammates with [[JT Thor]].{{cite web |last1=Hall |first1=Erik |title=Joshua Primo: 4 things to know about the Alabama men's basketball guard |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/2021/02/04/joshua-primo-facts-alabama-mens-basketball-guard/4397972001/ |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=February 4, 2021}} He transferred to Royal Crown Academic School in [[Scarborough, Toronto]].{{cite web |last1=Mikre |first1=Mickias |title=Joshua Primo Returns to Canada, Commits to Royal Crown |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2020/01/10/joshua-primo-returns-to-canada-commits-to-royal-crown/ |website=North Pole Hoops |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=January 10, 2020}} Primo reclassified to the 2020 class and graduated early.{{cite web |last1=Blackwell |first1=Joey |title=Freshman Guard Josh Primo Already Developing into Solid Contributor for Alabama Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/josh-primo-already-contributing-for-alabama-basketball-blackwell |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=December 11, 2020}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], choosing the Crimson Tide over [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |last1=South |first1=Hank |title=Five-star guard Josh Primo signs with Alabama |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Recruiting-Five-star-guard-Josh-Primo-signs-with-Tide-Nate-Oats--146078782/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=April 15, 2020}} ==College career== In his freshman season, Primo was the youngest player in college basketball. He averaged 8.1 points and 3.4 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Alabama's Joshua Primo to enter NBA draft but stay eligible to return to Crimson Tide |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31300916/alabama-joshua-primo-enter-draft-stay-eligible-crimson-tide |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=April 21, 2021}} Primo missed three games with a left [[medial collateral ligament]] sprain.{{cite web |last1=Vitale |first1=Josh |title=Alabama basketball 'hoping' Joshua Primo can play in NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/03/14/joshua-primo-injury-alabama-basketball-nate-oats-ncaa-tournament-2021/4696316001/ |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=March 14, 2021}} On April 21, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Alabama guard Josh Primo makes NBA Draft decision |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/alabama-football/nba-draft-josh-primo-crimson-tide-basketball/ |website=Saturday Down South |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=April 21, 2021}} However on June 30, Primo announced he was remaining in the draft due to a strong performance at the NBA combine.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Alabama's Joshua Primo, projected first-round pick, opts to stay in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31741140/alabama-joshua-primo-projected-first-round-pick-opts-stay-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 1, 2021 |date=June 30, 2020}} ==National team career== Primo represented [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in Greece. At age 16, he was the youngest player on the team and averaged 4.2 points per game.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Canadian prospect Josh Primo commits to Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/28962200/canadian-prospect-josh-primo-commits-alabama |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=March 27, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Jordan |title=Getting to know Alabama basketball target Josh Primo |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/getting-to-know-alabama-basketball-target-josh-primo |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=February 20, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | 30 || 19 || 22.5 || .431 || .381 || .750 || 3.4 || .8 || .6 || .3 || 8.1 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Primo's older sister, Keshia, played college basketball at the [[University at Buffalo]], [[Coffeyville Community College]], and [[Southern Connecticut State University]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://rolltide.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/joshua--primo/6834 Alabama Crimson Tide bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Primo, Joshua}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Toronto]] [[Category:Canadian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
